realLifeExampleSummary: Nach der Wahl zwischen zwei ähnlich guten Kopfhörern wirkt das gewählte Modell plötzlich besser und das abgelehnte schlechter.
coverHeadline: WARUM REDEN WIR UNS DAS SCHÖN?
coverVisualThesis: A buyer defensively holds a chosen pair of headphones while still glancing back at an equally appealing rejected alternative, making the tension between choice and doubt visible.

flowTextMoments.text: WARUM REDEN WIR UNS DAS SCHÖN?

scenes.speechSection: Warum verteidigst du manchmal eine Entscheidung besonders stark, obwohl du selbst noch Zweifel daran hast?
scenes.viewerTakeaway: People can defend a choice more strongly when the choice still leaves them with visible doubt.
scenes.observableEvidence: In an electronics store, a young adult clutches a newly chosen blue pair of headphones and its receipt close to the chest while glancing back at a similarly appealing green pair still on display; a friend beside them gestures neutrally toward the alternative.
scenes.representationReason: The hook is about defensive behavior after a difficult choice, so posture, gaze and the relation to another person are the clearest evidence.
scenes.dominantRelation: The buyer visibly protects the chosen option while still looking back at the rejected alternative.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not use glowing brains, split heads or abstract energy to represent dissonance.

scenes.speechSection: Eine mögliche Erklärung ist kognitive Dissonanz.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The viewer learns the name of the mechanism without repeating the store interaction.
scenes.observableEvidence: The exact term is integrated large beside a purchase receipt, the chosen blue headphones and the rejected green pair in the same illustrated world.
scenes.representationReason: This beat names the concept, so one large exact term paired with the episode objects is clearer than another character scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: Concept term paired with the unresolved choice objects.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No cracked head, lightning bolt or surreal mind symbol.

scenes.speechSection: Sie beschreibt eine unangenehme Spannung, wenn Überzeugungen, Entscheidungen oder Verhalten nicht gut zusammenpassen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Dissonance is about an uncomfortable mismatch between cognitions, choices or behavior.
scenes.observableEvidence: A simple three-part illustrated mechanism shows a balanced comparison of two headphones, the hand choosing the blue pair, then the buyer still looking back toward the green pair while holding the receipt.
scenes.representationReason: The definition describes a relation between choice and lingering inconsistency, which a simple three-step mechanism can show without abstract symbols.
scenes.dominantRelation: Choice is completed, but attention still returns to the attractive rejected option.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No text labels, brain icons, cracks or dense arrows.

scenes.speechSection: Du stehst zum Beispiel zwischen zwei ähnlich guten Kopfhörern, kaufst Modell A und lässt Modell B liegen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A difficult everyday choice between similar products can create the setup for post-choice dissonance.
scenes.observableEvidence: Top-down electronics counter with two equally prominent generic over-ear headphones, one matte blue and one muted green, beside one hand reaching decisively for the blue pair while the green pair remains close by.
scenes.representationReason: The choice itself is the point; the two products and the selecting hand communicate it faster than a full-body scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: One of two similarly attractive alternatives is selected.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable brand names, price labels or packaging text.

scenes.speechSection: Danach fallen dir plötzlich besonders die Vorteile von A und die Nachteile von B auf.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: After choosing, attention can shift toward reasons supporting the chosen option and against the rejected one.
scenes.observableEvidence: One coherent split comparison: left, the chosen blue headphones are examined closely for comfortable padding and solid build; right, the rejected green headphones are pushed slightly away while a small ordinary flaw in the hinge draws the buyer's attention.
scenes.representationReason: The beat explicitly contrasts post-choice attention to positive versus negative features, so a two-state comparison is the clearest evidence.
scenes.dominantRelation: Chosen option receives favorable inspection while rejected option receives critical inspection.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not use thumbs-up/down icons, stars, scores or readable labels.

scenes.speechSection: Genau solche Veränderungen nach Entscheidungen untersuchte Jack Brehm bereits 1956.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Post-decision evaluation shifts were tested experimentally decades ago.
scenes.observableEvidence: A 1950s psychology research room with plain furniture and several household consumer items arranged on a table; one participant evaluates the items while a researcher records responses on a clipboard.
scenes.representationReason: The historical study setup and consumer-choice context are the evidence, so the environment and props should carry the frame.
scenes.dominantRelation: Participant evaluates several consumer alternatives in a controlled 1950s study setting.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No modern devices, readable brands or contemporary clothing.

scenes.speechSection: Nach einer Wahl wurde das gewählte Produkt oft positiver und das abgelehnte negativer bewertet als zuvor.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The classic decision paradigm compared evaluations before and after making a choice.
scenes.observableEvidence: A simple three-stage tabletop sequence: several consumer-item cards are first arranged on a desirability board, then one of two close alternatives is chosen, then the same two cards are placed again with the chosen card moved upward and the rejected card downward.
scenes.representationReason: The result depends on before-choice versus after-choice evaluation, so a compact three-stage physical ranking sequence is clearer than another researcher scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: The chosen item moves upward in evaluation while the rejected item moves downward after choice.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No invented numbers, percentages, labels or corporate chart styling.

scenes.speechSection: Diese Verschiebung wird häufig als eine Form von Dissonanzreduktion nach einer Entscheidung interpretiert.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The post-choice shift is commonly interpreted as reducing inconsistency after a difficult decision.
scenes.observableEvidence: One direct before-versus-after comparison of the same two generic product cards: before the choice they sit at nearly equal height on a physical ranking board; after the choice the selected card is placed higher and the rejected card lower.
scenes.representationReason: The interpretation is anchored in a visible evaluation shift, so the same physical ranking setup before and after makes the change immediately readable.
scenes.dominantRelation: Near-equal alternatives become more separated after the choice.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable scales, percentages or abstract brain graphics.

scenes.speechSection: Ein zweiter Klassiker von Festinger und Carlsmith aus dem Jahr 1959 untersuchte erzwungene Zustimmung.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Another classic line of research examined inconsistency between what people did and what they privately thought.
scenes.observableEvidence: A late-1950s psychology lab with a repetitive wooden peg-and-spool task apparatus on a table, a stopwatch, plain chairs and a waiting area visible through an open doorway.
scenes.representationReason: The forced-compliance paradigm is best established by its distinctive repetitive task and period laboratory rather than another talking-head scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: A visibly tedious repetitive task sits at the center of a period laboratory setup.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable study title, modern electronics or invented signage.

scenes.speechSection: Teilnehmende erledigten eine langweilige Aufgabe und sollten danach einer anderen Person sagen, sie sei interessant.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Participants were asked to tell another person that a dull task was interesting.
scenes.observableEvidence: In the 1950s lab doorway, one participant who has just completed the peg task speaks with deliberately upbeat hand gestures to a waiting participant, while the boring apparatus remains clearly visible behind them.
scenes.representationReason: The key evidence is saying something socially positive that conflicts with the dull task just experienced, so the interaction itself is necessary.
scenes.dominantRelation: One participant presents the dull task enthusiastically to the next participant.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No speech-bubble text; show the mismatch through gesture and the visible task.
scenes.camera: medium doorway interaction with lab depth

scenes.speechSection: Wer dafür nur einen kleinen Anreiz bekam, bewertete die Aufgabe später positiver als Teilnehmende mit einem großen Anreiz.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: In the classic study, the small-incentive condition later evaluated the task more positively than the large-incentive condition.
scenes.observableEvidence: A clean two-state comparison using the same boring peg apparatus: left, one participant receives a single small coin/token and later gives a mildly positive evaluation gesture; right, another receives a thick cash envelope and later remains visibly unimpressed.
scenes.representationReason: The claim contrasts two incentive conditions and their later evaluations, so a restrained two-state comparison is the clearest form.
scenes.dominantRelation: Small external incentive is paired with a more positive later evaluation than a large external incentive.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not show exact dollar amounts, invented scores or readable forms.
scenes.camera: two-state medium comparison with large subjects

scenes.speechSection: Die klassische Erklärung: Bei geringer äußerer Rechtfertigung passten Verhalten und eigene Einstellung schlechter zusammen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: A small external justification leaves a larger mismatch between the dull experience and the positive statement.
scenes.observableEvidence: One simple three-part mechanism: the dull peg task, then a single small reward token beside the participant making an upbeat gesture to the waiting person, then the participant alone considering the task afterward.
scenes.representationReason: The sentence explains the logic of the classic interpretation, so one compact sequence of task, weak justification and later reconsideration is clearer than more dialogue.
scenes.dominantRelation: Weak external justification leaves the participant with more reason to reconcile the positive statement internally.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No brain icons, lightning, scales, labels or dense arrow networks.

scenes.speechSection: Eine Möglichkeit, diese Spannung zu reduzieren, ist die eigene Bewertung nachträglich zu verändern.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Changing one's own evaluation is one possible way to reduce the mismatch.
scenes.observableEvidence: At home, the recurring buyer places the chosen blue headphones prominently on the desk and closes a comparison page showing the rejected green pair, while the purchase receipt stays nearby.
scenes.representationReason: The beat is about shifting evaluation of the choice; the handling and placement of the chosen versus rejected option can show this without another argument scene.
scenes.dominantRelation: Chosen product is brought forward while the rejected comparison is deliberately closed away.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable web text, scores, glowing effects or symbolic brain imagery.

scenes.speechSection: Aber Dissonanztheorie ist kein Gedankenleser: Nicht jede Rechtfertigung oder Meinungsänderung lässt sich damit erklären.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Not every change in opinion or justification should automatically be labeled cognitive dissonance.
scenes.observableEvidence: Close object-led counterexample: the chosen blue headphones now have a clearly broken hinge on the desk, and the buyer's hand turns them over beside the receipt, giving a concrete new reason to change the evaluation.
scenes.representationReason: A real new piece of evidence is a clean counterexample showing that opinions can change for reasons other than dissonance.
scenes.dominantRelation: New external evidence, a broken hinge, provides a direct reason for reevaluation.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: Do not add labels explaining the lesson; the broken object must carry the point.

scenes.speechSection: Moderne Übersichten diskutieren weiterhin Messprobleme, unterschiedliche Paradigmen und offene theoretische Fragen.
scenes.viewerTakeaway: Modern discussion of cognitive dissonance includes measurement and conceptual challenges.
scenes.observableEvidence: A modern social-psychology research workspace with several distinct but simple task setups on separate tables, blank questionnaires, recording equipment and researchers comparing materials rather than one single standardized apparatus.
scenes.representationReason: The beat concerns methodological variety and measurement challenges, so a modern research environment with multiple paradigms is more concrete than an abstract warning card.
scenes.dominantRelation: Different experimental setups sit side by side, making lack of one simple universal measurement method visible.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No readable paper titles, charts, statistics or corporate infographic layout.

scenes.speechSection: Wenn du eine Wahl plötzlich extrem verteidigst, lohnt sich die Frage: Überzeugt sie mich – oder beruhige ich gerade meine Entscheidung?
scenes.viewerTakeaway: The practical takeaway is to distinguish genuine conviction from post-choice self-justification.
scenes.observableEvidence: Top-down illustrated desk with the chosen blue headphones, purchase receipt and the rejected green comparison image pushed to the edge; one large note card carries the final question.
scenes.representationReason: The closing beat is explicitly a reflective question, so one large exact phrase over the episode's concrete objects is the strongest ending.
scenes.dominantRelation: The final question sits between the chosen object and the evidence of the rejected alternative.
scenes.literalMetaphorWarning: No extra labels or explanatory paragraph.
